TreeletHub runs on your Mac as a honeycomb launcher for favorite apps and shortcuts. Pair this phone on the same Wi‑Fi to launch those Mac apps remotely. Layout stays in sync.
Keep TreeletHub running on the desk Mac. From the couch or another room, use your phone as a remote launcher for apps you already pinned on the Mac hub.

0) Install the Mac app first (website DMG)—this phone app alone cannot launch Mac apps.
1) On the Mac, open TreeletHub and read the six-digit pairing code.
2) On this phone, open Connect to Mac, type the code, then tap Connect.
3) If discovery fails, check Wi‑Fi, turn off VPN, and stay on the same network as the Mac.

1) Tap + on the Mac (or the dashed + on the honeycomb) to add an app, web shortcut, or system action.
2) Pinch to zoom, drag to pan; Control-click a tile to remove it.
3) Free plan includes up to 10 apps; unlock Pro once for unlimited slots.
4) If you regenerate the pairing code on the Mac, each phone must reconnect with the new code.
5) On Mac, open Settings (gear) for Dynamic Island, Keyboard Launcher, and Pro unlock.
Use the Apps tab for the live launcher synced from the Mac. In Settings, rename how your phone appears on the Mac, change the backdrop, or swap your one saved photo background.

Put ChatGPT, Codex, or Cursor into the hub grid, then tap it on iPhone: instead of just launching the app, your phone becomes a dedicated controller for that agent, and the whole vibe-coding loop moves into your hand. Kick off a run, approve or redirect what the agent proposes, tune how hard it thinks, and jump between chat, edits, and the terminal — the model keeps working while you stay in the flow, phone in hand and away from the keyboard.\nChatGPT, Codex, and Cursor each get a layout tuned to how you actually drive them, and every control is remappable to fit your workflow.\nThe Mac needs Accessibility and Automation permission for TreeletHub — without it the controller shows a warning and the keys do nothing.
On the Apps grid while paired: swipe down with two fingers to hide every open Mac app—including TreeletHub—and show the desktop.

Off by default. Some actions have no real shortcut, so TreeletHub types them into the command palette. If the palette fails to open, that text lands in the chat composer instead — keep this off unless you have verified it works.

Put ChatGPT, Codex, or Cursor into the Mac launcher, then tap it on this phone: instead of only launching the app, you open a control pad—status lights, command keys, joystick, and reasoning dial. Hold PTT to dictate on the phone; release to fill the Mac composer. Mac needs Accessibility and Automation for TreeletHub.
On the Apps launcher while paired: swipe down with two fingers to hide every open Mac app—including TreeletHub—and show the desktop.
While paired, swipe left or right across the hub pages (and Settings) to switch tabs, or tap the bottom bar.

With Pro unlocked on Mac, turn on Dynamic Island in the main window or gear menu. The floating strip can show media, pairing code / file staging, clipboard, synced launcher, clock, and weather (needs Location).
With Pro unlocked on Mac, enable Keyboard Launcher and allow Input Monitoring. Release Control for the on-screen keymap; Control + key launches mapped apps globally.

Free: up to 10 apps on Mac. One-time Pro unlock ($9.99, not a subscription) removes the limit and unlocks Dynamic Island, Keyboard Launcher, and other Pro features. Mac unlock status can sync to paired phones.
